name: ChatGPT Codex
description: OpenAI Codex as a chat agent: models and effort from the Codex CLI, sandbox modes, /review, /init, /mcp and your own prompts, session fork, export and delete, context meter, profiles and quick actions. Ships executable code.
author: Lumen

settings.label: Path to codex
settings.hint: Leave empty to find codex on the PATH and in the usual folders.

settings.label: Profile from config.toml
settings.hint: A profile that applies to every message: a [profiles.<name>] table in ~/.codex/config.toml or a ~/.codex/<name>.config.toml file. /profiles in the chat lists what Codex found.

settings.label: Default model
settings.hint: Applies while "Default" is chosen in the chat — e.g. gpt-5-codex. The chat picker comes from Codex itself.

settings.label: Model list from
settings.hint: "Automatic" reads ~/.codex/models_cache.json and asks codex app-server when the file is missing or you reload.

settings.label: Offer older and hidden models
settings.hint: Also adds models that Codex hides in its own list.

settings.label: More models
settings.hint: In addition to the Codex list — one model ID per line, optionally with "| Display name".

settings.label: Default reasoning effort
settings.hint: Applies while no effort is chosen in the chat. In the chat it can be set per model — only the levels the model supports are offered.

settings.label: Instructions for every chat
settings.placeholder: Answer briefly. Prefer small, reviewable changes.
settings.hint: Added to AGENTS.md as developer instructions. A system prompt set for one chat is added after it.

settings.label: Hand instructions to Codex
settings.hint: Exec mode has no system-prompt flag. "As developer_instructions" uses the config key of that name; use "In front of each message" if your Codex version ignores it.

settings.label: Web search
settings.hint: Sets web_search for the session (`--search` exists only in interactive Codex).

settings.label: Network in "In project" sandbox mode
settings.hint: Whether commands in the "In project" mode may access the network (npm install, curl …).

settings.label: Keep /tmp and $TMPDIR out of the writable roots
settings.hint: In "In project" mode Codex may also write to the temporary folders; this switches that off (sandbox_workspace_write.exclude_*).

settings.label: Approval policy (all modes)
settings.hint: Codex cannot ask questions in the chat — what it may do is set by the sandbox mode. "Never ask" keeps Codex from waiting for an answer. The per-mode settings below override this.

settings.label: Allow "Full access" mode
settings.hint: Warning: without a sandbox Codex can change any file and run any command. Use only in isolated environments.

settings.label: More writable folders
settings.hint: One per line.

settings.label: More configuration (-c)
settings.hint: One key=value per line in TOML format, as with `codex -c`. Lines starting with # are comments; lines that are not key=value are ignored (and reported in the chat).

settings.label: Environment variables
settings.hint: KEY=VALUE, one per line.

settings.label: Ephemeral sessions
settings.hint: --ephemeral: Codex keeps no session file. The chat cannot be resumed later, and Fork and Export do not work.

settings.label: Reply schema (--output-schema)
settings.hint: A JSON Schema file; Codex's final answer then follows that shape.

settings.label: Feature flags
settings.hint: One per line: a name enables the feature (--enable), a leading - disables it (--disable). `codex features list` shows them.

settings.label: Use a local model (--oss)
settings.hint: Runs against a local open-source provider instead of OpenAI.

settings.label: Quick actions
settings.default:
# Label | prompt   ({{selection}}, {{file}}, {{clipboard}}; \n is a line break)
Explain selection | Explain {{selection}} from {{file}} step by step.
Fix this file | Find and fix bugs in {{file}}. Explain each change briefly.
Write tests | Write tests for {{selection}} in {{file}} following the project's conventions, then run them.
Review changes | Review the uncommitted changes in this repository for bugs, risky changes and missing tests.
Commit message | Read the staged changes (git diff --staged) and write a concise conventional commit message. Do not commit.
settings.hint: Buttons above the message box. One per line: Label | prompt.

settings.label: Slash commands
settings.default:
# name | description | prompt   ($ARGUMENTS or {{args}} is what follows the command)
explain | Explain code or a concept | Explain $ARGUMENTS in simple terms, with an example from this project.
tests | Write tests | Write tests for $ARGUMENTS and run them. Follow the existing test style.
fix | Fix a problem | Find the cause of this problem and fix it: $ARGUMENTS
docs | Document code | Write or improve documentation comments for $ARGUMENTS.
refactor | Refactor | Refactor $ARGUMENTS for readability without changing behaviour; run the tests afterwards.
settings.hint: One per line: name | description | prompt. /review, /init, /status, /mcp and your ~/.codex/prompts are offered besides.

settings.label: Profiles
settings.default:
# Label | mode=… | model=… | effort=… | anySettingKey=value
Quick | mode=workspace-write | effort=low | reasoningSummary=none
Offline | mode=workspace-write | networkAccess=false | webSearch=disabled
Full access (needs the setting) | mode=danger-full-access | effort=medium
settings.hint: Presets for mode, model, effort and any setting of this extension. Full access works only when it is allowed above.

agents.name: Codex
agents.description: Ask Codex about your project: explain code, find bugs, make changes. What Codex may do is set by the mode.
agents.placeholder: Message Codex …  (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for a new line, @ files)

modes.label: In project
modes.description: Reads everything, changes and runs only in the project folder

modes.label: Full access
modes.description: No sandbox — must be enabled in the settings

suggestions: Explain the structure of this project.
Find possible bugs in the open file.
Write tests for the current selection.
